thread:
cheng: quick heads up — perf regression surfaced on nightly serving after the slab-change roll. p99 token latency increased for seq=512/1024 and we saw a couple of transient OOMs during our load test. attaching quick profiler output below

sasha: can you paste the numbers? which metric moved first?

cheng: profiler snippet:```
model: rdm-7b-v2
workload: chat-heavy, seq dist skewed to 256/512
p99 tokens: 42ms -> 50ms (+19%)
mean tokens: 10ms -> 12ms (+20%)
gpu mem high-water: 17.8GB -> 19.6GB
OOMs: 0 -> 3 (during 15k qps burst)
slab_pool_hits: 78% -> 61%
evictions/sec: 2.1 -> 8.7
fragmentation_ratio: 0.12 -> 0.29
```

maria: hmm slab_pool_hits dropping is the red flag. looks like retention TTL we added keeps small slabs pinned and prevents reuse for logits/scratchpad alignment. causes fragmentation + bigger allocs fall back to new buffers.

ken: also saw KV cache interop issue — when a request transitions from short to long sequence (prefix growth) the allocator requests a larger workspace but alignment mismatch prevents reusing the old buffer, so we allocate new logits scratchpad and evict earlier small ones.

aj: idea: introduce a "slab handoff" key: prefer reuse if requested size <= slab_size * 1.25 and same model-variant + compatible dtype. reduces wasted splits.

cheng: agree. propose two-track plan: short-term mitigation to avoid OOMs, and longer-term redesign of slab eviction + retention heuristics.

maria: short-term mitigation suggestions:
- lower retention TTL from 60s -> 8s for models with heavy seq variance
- add soft-reserve: if free_mem < 1GB then throttle new large requests (503) with retry-after header
- force coalescing of tiny slabs into bigger free extents on idle GC pass

ken: add to that: on allocation miss, check last_alloc_owner and last_seq_len; if same owner and seq grew, try inplace reallocation path (grow in-place) before allocating new slab. fallback to eviction only if grow fails.

aj: batching heuristic tweak: group inflight requests by target_scratchpad_size then schedule batch kernels that can share a pinned slab. That will increase reuse and reduce transient allocs. basically sort-by-slab-key before forming GPU batch.

cheng: we need metrics to validate. suggested new counters:
- slab_hit_rate (per model, per slab_size)
- slab_evictions_total
- fragmentation_ratio (free_extents / total_allocated)
- grow_inplace_failures

sasha: also surface per-route OOM incidence in console with timeline; makes it easier for product owners to see which prompts cause jumps.

maria: small config prototype (will push as feature flag):```json
{"slab": {"retention_ttl_seconds": 8, "size_classes": [4096, 16384, 65536, 262144], "grow_inplace_enabled": true, "max_waste_ratio": 0.25}}
```

ken: we should also add an eviction score combining age, usage_count, and fragmentation_penalty. current LRU is hurting frequently-reused small slabs. score = 0.6*age_norm + 0.3*(1/usage_count) + 0.1*frag_penalty

infra-bot: load-test: nightly/2026-04-02 03:12:47 -> found 3 OOMs on rdm-7b-v2, flagged to eng-runtime team

cheng: canary plan:
- roll short-term TTL change behind ff:slab_ttl_8s to 5% of hosted traffic
- enable batching-by-slab-key in local cluster for 48h and measure slab_hit_rate
- add soft-reserve throttle in gateway for free_mem<1GB

aj: I'll implement batching ordering patch. quick pseudocode:```
def make_batches(requests):
  group = defaultdict(list)
  for r in requests:
    key = (r.model_variant, ceil_pow2(r.scratchpad_size))
    group[key].append(r)
  # within group, sort by seq_len desc to maximize kv-cache reuse
  batches = []
  for k, rs in group.items():
    batches += chunk(rs, target_batch_size)
  return batches
```

maria: I'll prototype TTL change and coalescing GC. can add metric slab_reuse_by_size.

ken: I'll add grow-inplace path + eviction score change. start local perf harness.

cheng: who can own the AB and dashboards so we can measure before/after? @sasha?

sasha: I can own dashboards and alerts. will add new charts to perf tab and create alert when slab_evictions/sec > 5 for any model in prod canary.

deploy-bot: canary deployed: eng-runtime/slab-ttl-8s -> canary cluster (5% traffic) at 1801234579

cheng: nice. next check at +2h and +24h. aim to revert if OOMs not reduced or p99 still elevated.

aj: one more note — quantized kernels expect tightly-packed scratchpads; we should tag slabs with kernel_compat bits to avoid reusing incompatible buffer layouts. keeps perf consistent.

maria: good call. that will prevent perf cliffs when a slab reused for a non-compat kernel. add kernel_compat mask to slab metadata.

cheng: ok team — action items: aj batching PR, ken grow-inplace + eviction score, maria TTL+GC, sasha dashboards. update this thread with results. thanks :thumbsup:

sasha: noted, will post initial dashboards at 1801234660 (eta)

maria: patch pushed to branch slab-evict-2026. infra will run harness tonight.

ken: local harness shows p99 down from 50ms->44ms with batching ordering + TTL change on sample workload (seq heavy). pushing perf numbers tomorrow.

cheng: excellent. close loop tomorrow after 24h canary.
